ip_top_stories.title: Informa begins separation process for Taylor & Francis
ip_top_stories.summary: Informa has begun the process of separating its Taylor & Francis academic publishing division from the parent company. The move signals a significant structural change for one of the world's largest academic publishers, which has been at the centre of debates over AI licensing and content use.

ip_top_stories.title: NYT, AFP, The Economist join 40+ publishers to stop AI firms monetising content without permission
ip_top_stories.summary: The New York Times, AFP, The Economist and more than 40 other publishers have joined a coalition — SPUR — to resist AI companies using their content without payment or permission. The group is calling for enforceable standards to prevent AI firms from monetising publisher content without licensing agreements.

ip_top_stories.title: Microsoft knows it robbed publishers to train AI. It just doesn't care
ip_top_stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Microsoft knowingly used publisher content to train its AI systems without compensation, and that the company's scale and influence have allowed it to sidestep meaningful accountability. The article draws on reporting about the broader pattern of AI companies treating copyright as an obstacle rather than a legal constraint.

ip_top_stories.title: The Questions AI Copyright Cases Need to Answer
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis piece examines the key unresolved legal questions that courts will need to settle in ongoing AI copyright litigation, including issues around training data, fair use, and the status of AI-generated outputs. The article outlines how different rulings could set precedents with sweeping consequences for the AI industry and rights holders.

ip_top_stories.title: AI companies' book hunt sparks copyright concerns in Türkiye's publishing industry
ip_top_stories.summary: Turkish publishers are raising concerns after AI companies have been actively seeking access to book content for training data, prompting debate about whether adequate copyright protections exist. The story reflects a growing global pattern of AI firms targeting publishing catalogues without established licensing frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Global publishers form SPUR coalition to protect content from AI misuse
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers worldwide have formed the SPUR coalition to establish coordinated resistance to AI companies using journalistic and publishing content without permission or payment.

ip_further_links.title: Global creative bodies launch ethical AI charter 'in the vacuum of government policy'
ip_further_links.summary: International creative industry organisations have launched an ethical AI charter aimed at setting standards for AI use of creative content, citing a lack of adequate government action.

ip_further_links.title: A $1.5 Billion Warning: What 'Bartz' Means for AI Companies
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of the Bartz case examines how a $1.5 billion ruling could reshape liability exposure for AI companies in copyright disputes.

ip_further_links.title: Reddit and Perplexity AI clash over law firm's role in data-scraping case
ip_further_links.summary: Reddit and Perplexity AI are in dispute over the role of a law firm representing both parties in a data-scraping lawsuit, raising conflict-of-interest concerns in AI copyright litigation.

ip_further_links.title: Pope's AI adviser warns Australia's copyright changes risk 'new form of colonialism'
ip_further_links.summary: A senior adviser to the Pope on AI issues has warned that proposed Australian copyright reforms allowing AI training on protected content could constitute a new form of digital colonialism, disadvantaging smaller nations and creators.

ip_further_links.title: Australian voters back AI copyright changes — if creators get paid
ip_further_links.summary: A survey finds that Australian voters are broadly supportive of AI copyright reform, but only on condition that creators receive compensation when their work is used for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: From Goncourt to AI: Rethinking Authorship and Copyright in French Law
ip_further_links.summary: A legal analysis piece examines how French copyright law is being challenged to adapt to questions of AI authorship, drawing on the country's strong author-rights tradition.

ip_further_links.title: AI Video Game Mashups Are Going Viral, but Do They Cross the Line Into Copyright Infringement?
ip_further_links.summary: As AI-generated video game mashup content spreads across social media, legal commentators are debating whether such outputs constitute copyright infringement of the underlying game assets.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post – Artificial Intelligence in Scholarly Publishing: Are We Moving Faster Than the Evidence?
ip_further_links.summary: A guest post on The Scholarly Kitchen questions whether the academic publishing industry is adopting AI tools ahead of robust evidence about their reliability, accuracy, and impact on research integrity.

ip_further_links.title: Media giants unite on AI copyright, 400 scientists demand international oversight body
ip_further_links.summary: Major media organisations have aligned on shared AI copyright demands while 400 scientists have separately called for an international body to oversee AI-generated content.
